s1.syndrome_frame: Chronic recurrent painful ulcerations of the lower limbs with livedo pattern
salient_findings: Recurrent painful ulcerations on both legs and feet
Reticular purplish livedo pattern over both lower limbs
Chronic nonhealing ulcers on the lateral malleolus and the dorsum of the foot
key_facts: 31-year-old woman
4-year history of recurrent painful ulcerations
No personal or family history of vascular or autoimmune disease
No arthralgia or other dermatologic symptoms
No tobacco or illicit drug use
Multiple chronic nonhealing ulcers on the lower limbs
White atrophic scars on the lower legs and ankles
Lesional skin biopsy was performed

shortlist.label: Antiphospholipid syndrome
shortlist.why_kept: Livedo pattern and recurrent ulcerations are consistent with antiphospholipid syndrome

shortlist.label: Polyarteritis nodosa
shortlist.why_kept: Chronic nonhealing ulcers and livedo pattern are compatible with polyarteritis nodosa

shortlist.label: Thromboangiitis obliterans
shortlist.why_kept: Recurrent painful ulcerations and absence of autoimmune disease history suggest thromboangiitis obliterans

shortlist.label: Protein C deficiency
shortlist.why_kept: Recurrent ulcerations and lack of other explanations make protein C deficiency a plausible consideration

shortlist.label: Cryoglobulinemia
shortlist.why_kept: Chronic ulcerations and livedo pattern can be seen in cryoglobulinemia, although less common

raw.rationale: The patient's age, sex, and history of recurrent painful ulcerations on the lower limbs, along with the absence of personal or family history of vascular or autoimmune disease, are consistent with Thromboangiitis obliterans. The presence of a reticular purplish livedo pattern and multiple chronic nonhealing ulcers also support this diagnosis.

rejected.label: Antiphospholipid syndrome
rejected.why: Typically associated with a personal or family history of vascular or autoimmune disease, which is not present in this case

rejected.label: Polyarteritis nodosa
rejected.why: Often presents with systemic symptoms such as arthralgia, which are not present in this case

rejected.label: Protein C deficiency
rejected.why: Typically presents with deep vein thrombosis, which is not mentioned in this case

rejected.label: Cryoglobulinemia
rejected.why: Often associated with other dermatologic symptoms, such as purpura, which are not present in this case
